summary: Gabriel Jouveau-Dubreuil (1885–1945) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Paris (~1910–1914) and served as Professor of “physique chimie” at the Lycée Français de Pondichéry in 1909.
Gabriele Zeller (b. 1956) is an Indologist who studied under Ulrich Schneider. She held posts at Selly Oak Colleges (attested 1998) and the University of Tübingen (attested 2000).

Gadjin Nagao (1907–2005) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University under Ryotai Hatani and Susumu Yamaguchi, later holding the Chair of Buddhist Studies at Kyoto University (1935–1971).

Gail Hinich Sutherland is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Chicago under advisers Carol Bolon and Wendy Doniger, and under traditional teacher Virendra Singh.

Galuh Nur Fattah works in Buddhist studies and philosophy, completing an M.Phil. at Gadjah Mada University (2021–2023). Fattah served as an assistant professor at Gadjah Mada University (2024–2025) and became a lecturer at Sekolah Tinggi Agama Buddha Negeri Raden Wijaya in 2025.

Gananath Obeyesekere (1930–2025) worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon and University of Washington, later teaching at Ceylon (~1958–1972), UC San Diego (~1972–1980), and Princeton University (1980–2000).

Ganesh Prasad (1876–1935) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the universities of Allahabad and Calcutta. He headed a department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1905) and held professorships at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Calcutta.

Ganganatha Jha (1872–1941) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Allahabad. He served as professor at Muir Central College (1902–1918), principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1918–1923), and vice chancellor of Allahabad University (1923–1932).

Gangzhun (b. 1971) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Qinghai Nationalities University and completed a master's degree at Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001) under the supervision of Alak Dorje Rinpoche.

Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008) and studied under traditional teacher Lama Byambaa.
Garab Dorje Rinpoche (b. 1967) is an active figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

Garcin de Tassy (1794–1878) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Collège de France under Louis-Mathieu Langlès, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and Jean Daniel Kieffer. He held the chair of Indian languages at INALCO from 1828 to 1877.

Gareth Fisher works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After completing a Ph.D. in socio-cultural anthropology at the University of Virginia (1999–2006), he joined Syracuse University in 2008 as Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology.

Gareth Sparham (b. 1948) works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and earned a Ph.D. from the University of British Columbia under Ashok Aklujkar, later lecturing in Tibetan at the University of Michigan (1999–2009).

Gary A. Tubb (b. 1950) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He taught at Columbia University and served as Professor, Chair, and later Professor Emeritus at the University of Chicago.

Gary D. DeAngelis works in religious and Buddhist studies, having studied under mentors including Masatoshi Nagatomi, George Rupp, and Herbert Mason. He served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).

Gary Donnelly specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Oxford, the University of Liverpool, and the University of Manchester, and held teaching roles at Liverpool (2016–2020) and Liverpool Hope University (2023).

Gary Goh Wee Kian is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under supervisors Hui-Chieh Loy and Jay L. Garfield, as well as teachers Brook Ziporyn, Christopher Anthony Brown, and Cecilia Lim.

Gary Snyder (b. 1930) is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Reed College, Indiana University, and UC Berkeley, trained under several traditional Zen teachers, and served as a professor at the University of California, Davis (1986–2002).

Gary Urton (b. 1946) is an anthropology and history scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. He held faculty posts at Colgate University (1978–2002) and served as Dumbarton Oaks Professor at Harvard University (~2002–2020).
